label: Rheum / Immuno
blurb: NSAIDs, DMARDs, biologics, immunosuppressants, transplant and allergy drugs

drugs.name: Ibuprofen
drugs.primaryEffect: Reduces pain, fever, and inflammation
drugs.treatmentUsage: Osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, acute pain, fever, dysmenorrhea, closure of patent ductus arteriosus in neonates
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Reversibly and nonselectively inhibits cyclooxygenase-1 and cyclooxygenase-2, reducing prostaglandin synthesis from arachidonic acid.
drugs.sideEffects: Gastric ulceration and bleeding, acute kidney injury, sodium and fluid retention, hypertension, increased cardiovascular events, interstitial nephritis
drugs.contraindications: Third trimester of pregnancy, active peptic ulcer, chronic kidney disease, heart failure, coronary artery bypass grafting perioperatively, aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease
drugs.tooltip: It competes with aspirin for the COX-1 site, so taking ibuprofen before aspirin blunts aspirin's cardioprotection. Renal injury occurs because prostaglandins maintain afferent arteriolar dilation.

drugs.name: Naproxen
drugs.primaryEffect: Long-acting anti-inflammatory and analgesic effect
drugs.treatmentUsage: Rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, acute gout, ankylosing spondylitis, migraine, dysmenorrhea
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Nonselectively and reversibly inhibits COX-1 and COX-2, reducing prostaglandin-mediated inflammation, pain sensitization, and fever with a long half-life allowing twice-daily dosing.
drugs.sideEffects: Gastrointestinal ulceration and bleeding, renal impairment, fluid retention, hypertension, tinnitus
drugs.contraindications: Active peptic ulcer, advanced chronic kidney disease, third trimester of pregnancy, perioperative CABG, heart failure
drugs.tooltip: Often preferred among NSAIDs in patients with cardiovascular risk because observational data suggest the lowest thrombotic signal. Still requires gastroprotection in high-risk patients.

drugs.name: Celecoxib
drugs.primaryEffect: Anti-inflammatory effect with reduced gastric toxicity
drugs.treatmentUsage: Osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, acute pain in patients at high gastrointestinal risk
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Selectively inhibits COX-2, the inducible isoform driving inflammation, while largely sparing COX-1 which maintains gastric mucosal prostaglandins and platelet thromboxane.
drugs.sideEffects: Cardiovascular thrombotic events, hypertension, renal impairment, edema; less gastrointestinal bleeding than nonselective NSAIDs
drugs.contraindications: Sulfa allergy, established cardiovascular disease, perioperative CABG, third trimester of pregnancy, severe renal impairment
drugs.tooltip: Sparing COX-1 preserves gastric protection but also leaves platelet thromboxane intact while suppressing endothelial prostacyclin — the imbalance that explains the prothrombotic risk.

drugs.name: Acetaminophen
drugs.primaryEffect: Relieves pain and fever without anti-inflammatory effect
drugs.treatmentUsage: Mild to moderate pain, fever, osteoarthritis, pain in patients where NSAIDs are contraindicated
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Inhibits cyclooxygenase primarily in the central nervous system where peroxide levels are low, and may act through cannabinoid and TRPV1 pathways; it has negligible peripheral anti-inflammatory effect.
drugs.sideEffects: Hepatotoxicity in overdose or with chronic alcohol use, rash; generally very well tolerated at therapeutic doses
drugs.contraindications: Severe hepatic impairment, doses above 3 to 4 grams daily, chronic heavy alcohol use requires lower limits
drugs.tooltip: Safe for the stomach, kidneys, and platelets, which is why it is first-line in the elderly and in anticoagulated patients. Toxicity comes from NAPQI when glutathione is depleted.

drugs.name: Prednisone
drugs.primaryEffect: Broad suppression of inflammation and immune activation
drugs.treatmentUsage: Rheumatoid arthritis flares, lupus, vasculitis, polymyalgia rheumatica, giant cell arteritis, asthma exacerbation, transplant rejection
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Prodrug converted to prednisolone, which binds the glucocorticoid receptor to inhibit NF-kB and AP-1, suppressing cytokine transcription and inducing lipocortin to block phospholipase A2.
drugs.sideEffects: Hyperglycemia, osteoporosis, avascular necrosis, immunosuppression, myopathy, cataracts, mood disturbance, adrenal suppression, Cushingoid habitus
drugs.contraindications: Systemic fungal infection, live vaccines; avoid abrupt discontinuation after more than three weeks of therapy
drugs.tooltip: Giant cell arteritis is treated immediately on suspicion, before biopsy, to prevent irreversible blindness. Anyone on more than three months of steroids needs calcium, vitamin D, and bone density monitoring.

drugs.name: Methotrexate (Rheumatology)
drugs.primaryEffect: Slows structural joint damage in inflammatory arthritis
drugs.treatmentUsage: Rheumatoid arthritis (anchor drug), psoriatic arthritis, psoriasis, juvenile idiopathic arthritis, ectopic pregnancy
drugs.mechanismOfAction: At low weekly doses it promotes adenosine release and inhibits AICAR transformylase, producing anti-inflammatory effects distinct from the antifolate cytotoxicity seen at chemotherapy doses.
drugs.sideEffects: Mucositis and stomatitis, hepatotoxicity, myelosuppression, pulmonary toxicity, nausea, alopecia, severe teratogenicity
drugs.contraindications: Pregnancy and conception attempts, significant liver disease, alcohol use, creatinine clearance below 30, pleural effusion or ascites, concurrent trimethoprim
drugs.tooltip: Dosed once weekly with daily folic acid supplementation, which reduces mucositis and hepatotoxicity without reducing efficacy. Weekly-versus-daily dosing errors have caused fatal pancytopenia.

drugs.name: Hydroxychloroquine
drugs.primaryEffect: Mild immunomodulation with a very favorable safety profile
drugs.treatmentUsage: Systemic lupus erythematosus (used in essentially all patients), rheumatoid arthritis, Sjogren syndrome, cutaneous lupus, malaria
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Accumulates in lysosomes and raises their pH, impairing antigen processing and Toll-like receptor 7 and 9 signaling, which reduces interferon-driven autoimmune activation.
drugs.sideEffects: Irreversible retinopathy with bull's-eye maculopathy, gastrointestinal upset, skin hyperpigmentation, myopathy, cardiomyopathy, QT prolongation
drugs.contraindications: Preexisting maculopathy, G6PD deficiency with caution; requires baseline and annual ophthalmologic screening after five years
drugs.tooltip: Given to nearly every lupus patient because it reduces flares, thrombosis, and mortality and is safe in pregnancy. Annual retinal screening is required because the retinopathy is irreversible.

drugs.name: Sulfasalazine
drugs.primaryEffect: Reduces joint and bowel inflammation
drugs.treatmentUsage: Rheumatoid arthritis, peripheral arthritis of spondyloarthritis, ulcerative colitis
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Colonic bacteria cleave the azo bond releasing sulfapyridine, which provides the systemic antirheumatic effect, and 5-aminosalicylate, which acts topically on bowel mucosa.
drugs.sideEffects: Nausea, headache, rash, reversible oligospermia, hemolysis in G6PD deficiency, agranulocytosis, folate deficiency, orange-yellow discoloration of urine and skin
drugs.contraindications: Sulfa or salicylate allergy, G6PD deficiency, porphyria, intestinal or urinary obstruction
drugs.tooltip: One of the few DMARDs considered safe in pregnancy, though folate supplementation is essential. Reversible oligospermia is a distinctive counseling point for male patients.

drugs.name: Leflunomide
drugs.primaryEffect: Suppresses lymphocyte proliferation in inflammatory arthritis
drugs.treatmentUsage: Rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, especially when methotrexate is not tolerated
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Its active metabolite inhibits dihydroorotate dehydrogenase, blocking de novo pyrimidine synthesis on which activated lymphocytes depend for clonal expansion.
drugs.sideEffects: Diarrhea, hepatotoxicity, hypertension, alopecia, peripheral neuropathy, myelosuppression, severe teratogenicity
drugs.contraindications: Pregnancy (boxed warning), significant liver disease; requires cholestyramine washout before conception because the metabolite persists for up to two years
drugs.tooltip: The enterohepatic recirculation of its active metabolite means it lingers for up to two years. Cholestyramine washout is required before pregnancy or in cases of toxicity.

drugs.name: Adalimumab
drugs.primaryEffect: Blocks TNF-driven inflammation across autoimmune disease
drugs.treatmentUsage: Rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, Crohn disease, ulcerative colitis, hidradenitis suppurativa, uveitis
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Fully human monoclonal antibody binding soluble and membrane-bound TNF-alpha, preventing it from engaging TNF receptors and driving inflammatory cascades.
drugs.sideEffects: Reactivation of latent tuberculosis and hepatitis B, serious bacterial and fungal infection, injection site reactions, drug-induced lupus, demyelinating disease, lymphoma
drugs.contraindications: Active infection, untreated latent tuberculosis, moderate to severe heart failure, demyelinating disease, live vaccines
drugs.tooltip: Screen for latent tuberculosis with an interferon-gamma release assay and for hepatitis B before starting. TNF maintains granulomas, so blocking it lets walled-off tuberculosis disseminate.

drugs.name: Etanercept
drugs.primaryEffect: Neutralizes TNF using a soluble receptor decoy
drugs.treatmentUsage: Rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, plaque psoriasis, juvenile idiopathic arthritis
drugs.mechanismOfAction: A fusion protein of two soluble TNF receptor p75 domains linked to an IgG1 Fc region that acts as a decoy receptor, binding and neutralizing circulating TNF-alpha and lymphotoxin.
drugs.sideEffects: Injection site reactions, infection including tuberculosis reactivation, drug-induced lupus, demyelinating disease, malignancy risk
drugs.contraindications: Active infection, untreated latent tuberculosis, heart failure, demyelinating disease, live vaccines
drugs.tooltip: Unlike the antibody TNF inhibitors, etanercept is a decoy receptor and is notably ineffective in granulomatous disease such as Crohn disease and sarcoidosis — a frequently tested distinction.

drugs.name: Tocilizumab
drugs.primaryEffect: Blocks interleukin-6 driven inflammation
drugs.treatmentUsage: Rheumatoid arthritis, giant cell arteritis, systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis, cytokine release syndrome from CAR-T therapy, severe COVID-19
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Monoclonal antibody against the interleukin-6 receptor, blocking both membrane-bound and soluble IL-6 signaling that drives acute phase reactants and synovial inflammation.
drugs.sideEffects: Elevated transaminases and lipids, neutropenia, gastrointestinal perforation especially in diverticulitis, infection, suppressed CRP masking infection
drugs.contraindications: Active infection, diverticulitis or prior gastrointestinal perforation, absolute neutrophil count below 2000, active hepatic disease
drugs.tooltip: Because IL-6 drives CRP production, tocilizumab normalizes CRP even during active infection — so inflammatory markers cannot be trusted to detect sepsis in these patients.

drugs.name: Abatacept
drugs.primaryEffect: Prevents full T cell activation
drugs.treatmentUsage: Rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, polyarticular juvenile idiopathic arthritis
drugs.mechanismOfAction: A CTLA-4 and IgG Fc fusion protein that binds CD80 and CD86 on antigen-presenting cells with high affinity, denying CD28 the second signal T cells require for activation.
drugs.sideEffects: Infection including tuberculosis reactivation, infusion reactions, headache, exacerbation of COPD, malignancy risk
drugs.contraindications: Active infection, untreated latent tuberculosis; avoid combining with TNF inhibitors because infection risk multiplies
drugs.tooltip: A direct application of the two-signal model of T cell activation: signal one is the MHC-TCR interaction, signal two is CD28 binding CD80/86. Abatacept blocks signal two.

drugs.name: Tofacitinib
drugs.primaryEffect: Blocks intracellular cytokine signaling
drugs.treatmentUsage: Rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, ulcerative colitis, ankylosing spondylitis, alopecia areata
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Inhibits Janus kinases 1 and 3, blocking STAT phosphorylation downstream of multiple cytokine receptors and thereby suppressing a broad range of inflammatory signals.
drugs.sideEffects: Herpes zoster reactivation, serious infection, thrombosis and pulmonary embolism, major cardiovascular events, malignancy, elevated lipids and creatine kinase, cytopenias
drugs.contraindications: Active infection, untreated latent tuberculosis, prior thrombosis, age over 50 with cardiovascular risk factors (boxed warning), severe hepatic impairment
drugs.tooltip: An oral small molecule rather than an injectable biologic. The boxed warnings for thrombosis, cardiovascular events, and malignancy restrict it to patients who have failed a TNF inhibitor.

drugs.name: Belimumab
drugs.primaryEffect: Reduces autoreactive B cell survival in lupus
drugs.treatmentUsage: Systemic lupus erythematosus with active disease despite standard therapy; lupus nephritis
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Binds B lymphocyte stimulator (BLyS or BAFF), preventing it from supporting survival and differentiation of autoreactive B cells into autoantibody-producing plasma cells.
drugs.sideEffects: Infection, infusion and hypersensitivity reactions, depression and suicidality, nausea, diarrhea, progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy rarely
drugs.contraindications: Severe active lupus nephritis or CNS lupus historically, live vaccines, active severe infection
drugs.tooltip: The first drug approved for lupus in over fifty years. BLyS levels correlate with lupus disease activity, making it a rational target for reducing autoantibody production.

drugs.name: Anakinra
drugs.primaryEffect: Blocks interleukin-1 mediated inflammation
drugs.treatmentUsage: Rheumatoid arthritis, cryopyrin-associated periodic syndromes, adult-onset Still disease, refractory gout, pericarditis, macrophage activation syndrome
drugs.mechanismOfAction: A recombinant form of the natural interleukin-1 receptor antagonist that competitively blocks IL-1 alpha and IL-1 beta from binding the IL-1 type 1 receptor.
drugs.sideEffects: Injection site reactions (very common), neutropenia, serious infection, headache, elevated transaminases
drugs.contraindications: Active infection, neutropenia; avoid combining with TNF inhibitors due to infection risk
drugs.tooltip: IL-1 is the product of inflammasome activation, so anakinra is the treatment for autoinflammatory syndromes and for gout when NSAIDs, colchicine, and steroids are all contraindicated.

drugs.name: Secukinumab
drugs.primaryEffect: Blocks the IL-17 axis driving psoriatic inflammation
drugs.treatmentUsage: Plaque psoriasis, psoriatic arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, non-radiographic axial spondyloarthritis
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Monoclonal antibody that binds interleukin-17A, preventing it from engaging the IL-17 receptor on keratinocytes and synoviocytes and driving neutrophilic inflammation.
drugs.sideEffects: Mucocutaneous candidiasis, upper respiratory infection, new onset or exacerbation of inflammatory bowel disease, neutropenia
drugs.contraindications: Active Crohn disease or ulcerative colitis (it can worsen them), active infection, live vaccines
drugs.tooltip: IL-17 is essential for mucosal antifungal defense, which is why candidiasis is the signature side effect — the same reason IL-17 pathway defects cause chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis.

drugs.name: Azathioprine (Rheumatology)
drugs.primaryEffect: Suppresses lymphocyte proliferation for maintenance therapy
drugs.treatmentUsage: Lupus nephritis maintenance, ANCA vasculitis maintenance, autoimmune hepatitis, myasthenia gravis, steroid-sparing therapy
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Converted to 6-mercaptopurine and then thioguanine nucleotides, which incorporate into DNA and inhibit de novo purine synthesis, preferentially affecting proliferating lymphocytes.
drugs.sideEffects: Myelosuppression, hepatotoxicity, pancreatitis, increased lymphoma and skin cancer risk, nausea, infection
drugs.contraindications: Concurrent allopurinol or febuxostat without a 75 percent dose reduction, TPMT or NUDT15 deficiency, prior azathioprine pancreatitis
drugs.tooltip: One of the few immunosuppressants considered acceptable in pregnancy, because the fetal liver lacks the enzyme to convert it to the active metabolite. Check TPMT before starting.

drugs.name: Cyclophosphamide (Rheumatology)
drugs.primaryEffect: Rapid and profound suppression of autoimmune activity
drugs.treatmentUsage: Severe lupus nephritis, ANCA-associated vasculitis induction, scleroderma interstitial lung disease, organ-threatening or life-threatening autoimmune disease
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Hepatically activated to phosphoramide mustard, which cross-links DNA and kills proliferating lymphocytes, dramatically reducing autoantibody production.
drugs.sideEffects: Hemorrhagic cystitis and bladder cancer, myelosuppression, premature ovarian failure and male infertility, infection, secondary malignancy, SIADH
drugs.contraindications: Pregnancy, severe marrow suppression, active severe infection, urinary outflow obstruction
drugs.tooltip: Reserved for organ-threatening disease because of infertility and malignancy risk. Mesna and hydration prevent hemorrhagic cystitis; gonadal protection with leuprolide is often offered.

drugs.name: Mycophenolate Mofetil (Rheumatology)
drugs.primaryEffect: Selective suppression of lymphocyte proliferation
drugs.treatmentUsage: Lupus nephritis induction and maintenance, scleroderma interstitial lung disease, vasculitis maintenance, transplant rejection prophylaxis
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Inhibits inosine monophosphate dehydrogenase, blocking de novo guanosine synthesis; lymphocytes are selectively affected because they lack a purine salvage pathway.
drugs.sideEffects: Diarrhea and gastrointestinal intolerance, leukopenia, anemia, CMV and BK virus infection, severe teratogenicity, lymphoma risk
drugs.contraindications: Pregnancy (boxed warning), hypersensitivity; requires effective contraception and pregnancy testing
drugs.tooltip: Now preferred over cyclophosphamide for lupus nephritis with comparable efficacy and preserved fertility. Absolutely contraindicated in pregnancy, unlike azathioprine.

drugs.name: Tacrolimus (Transplant)
drugs.primaryEffect: Prevents T cell activation and allograft rejection
drugs.treatmentUsage: Solid organ transplant rejection prophylaxis, graft-versus-host disease, membranous nephropathy, atopic dermatitis topically
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Binds FKBP-12 and the complex inhibits calcineurin phosphatase, preventing NFAT dephosphorylation and blocking interleukin-2 transcription required for T cell clonal expansion.
drugs.sideEffects: Nephrotoxicity, tremor and neurotoxicity, new-onset diabetes after transplant, hypertension, hyperkalemia, hypomagnesemia, alopecia, QT prolongation
drugs.contraindications: Concurrent strong CYP3A4 modulators without level monitoring, hypersensitivity to the castor oil vehicle
drugs.tooltip: The standard transplant backbone with mycophenolate and prednisone. Grapefruit juice and azole antifungals inhibit CYP3A4 and cause toxic levels — a classic interaction question.

drugs.name: Sirolimus
drugs.primaryEffect: Blocks lymphocyte proliferation without nephrotoxicity
drugs.treatmentUsage: Transplant rejection prophylaxis especially when calcineurin nephrotoxicity is a concern, lymphangioleiomyomatosis, drug-eluting coronary stents, vascular anomalies
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Binds FKBP-12 and the complex inhibits the mechanistic target of rapamycin, arresting lymphocytes in G1 phase and preventing IL-2 driven proliferation.
drugs.sideEffects: Impaired wound healing, hyperlipidemia, mouth ulcers, proteinuria, interstitial pneumonitis, thrombocytopenia, lymphocele
drugs.contraindications: Immediately after transplant surgery because of impaired wound healing and hepatic artery thrombosis in liver transplant; hypersensitivity
drugs.tooltip: Binds the same FKBP-12 protein as tacrolimus but inhibits mTOR rather than calcineurin, so it blocks the response to IL-2 rather than its production. Not nephrotoxic, unlike calcineurin inhibitors.

drugs.name: Basiliximab
drugs.primaryEffect: Prevents early acute transplant rejection
drugs.treatmentUsage: Induction immunosuppression at the time of kidney and other solid organ transplantation
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Chimeric monoclonal antibody against CD25, the alpha chain of the interleukin-2 receptor on activated T cells, blocking IL-2 driven clonal expansion.
drugs.sideEffects: Generally well tolerated; hypersensitivity reactions, increased infection risk, gastrointestinal upset
drugs.contraindications: Hypersensitivity; live vaccines
drugs.tooltip: Used only for induction in the first days after transplant, not for maintenance. Because it targets only activated T cells expressing CD25, it causes far less global immunosuppression.

drugs.name: Antithymocyte Globulin
drugs.primaryEffect: Profoundly depletes circulating T lymphocytes
drugs.treatmentUsage: Induction in high-immunologic-risk transplant, treatment of steroid-resistant acute rejection, aplastic anemia
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Polyclonal rabbit or horse antibodies against multiple human T cell surface antigens that cause complement-mediated lysis and opsonization, depleting T cells for months.
drugs.sideEffects: Cytokine release syndrome with fever and rigors, serum sickness, thrombocytopenia and leukopenia, profound infection risk including CMV, post-transplant lymphoproliferative disease
drugs.contraindications: Active severe infection, prior severe reaction; requires premedication with steroids, acetaminophen, and antihistamine
drugs.tooltip: First-line for aplastic anemia in patients who are not transplant candidates, combined with cyclosporine. Serum sickness appears one to two weeks later as fever, rash, and arthralgias.

drugs.name: Epinephrine
drugs.primaryEffect: Reverses the physiology of anaphylaxis within minutes
drugs.treatmentUsage: Anaphylaxis (first-line), cardiac arrest, severe asthma refractory to other therapy, croup nebulized, septic shock refractory to other vasopressors
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Alpha-1 stimulation reverses vasodilation and mucosal edema, beta-1 increases cardiac output, and beta-2 causes bronchodilation and stabilizes mast cells against further degranulation.
drugs.sideEffects: Tachycardia, hypertension, anxiety, tremor, headache, myocardial ischemia in coronary disease, arrhythmias
drugs.contraindications: None in true anaphylaxis; caution in coronary artery disease; patients on beta-blockers may need glucagon if refractory
drugs.tooltip: Intramuscular into the anterolateral thigh is the route, because absorption is faster than subcutaneous or deltoid. Antihistamines and steroids are adjuncts and never substitutes.

drugs.name: Omalizumab (Allergy)
drugs.primaryEffect: Removes free IgE and desensitizes mast cells
drugs.treatmentUsage: Chronic spontaneous urticaria refractory to antihistamines, severe allergic asthma, nasal polyps, food allergy
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Binds the Fc portion of free IgE so it cannot engage the high-affinity FcepsilonRI receptor, which secondarily downregulates receptor density on mast cells and basophils.
drugs.sideEffects: Anaphylaxis (boxed warning), injection site reactions, arthralgia, headache, small increase in parasitic infection risk
drugs.contraindications: Hypersensitivity; not for acute allergic reactions or status asthmaticus
drugs.tooltip: Highly effective for chronic urticaria even when IgE levels are normal, suggesting mast cell receptor downregulation matters as much as IgE removal. Observation after early doses is required.

drugs.name: Cetirizine (Allergy)
drugs.primaryEffect: Blocks histamine-mediated allergic symptoms
drugs.treatmentUsage: Allergic rhinitis, chronic urticaria, allergic conjunctivitis, pruritus, adjunct in anaphylaxis after epinephrine
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Selective peripheral H1 receptor inverse agonist that stabilizes the inactive receptor conformation, reducing vascular permeability, pruritus, and mucus production.
drugs.sideEffects: Mild somnolence, dry mouth, headache, fatigue
drugs.contraindications: Hypersensitivity; requires renal dose adjustment
drugs.tooltip: In chronic urticaria, second-generation antihistamines are titrated up to four times the standard dose before adding omalizumab — a key step in the treatment algorithm.

drugs.name: Colchicine (Rheumatology)
drugs.primaryEffect: Blocks neutrophil-driven crystal inflammation
drugs.treatmentUsage: Acute gout flare, gout prophylaxis when starting urate-lowering therapy, familial Mediterranean fever, recurrent pericarditis, pseudogout
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Binds tubulin and prevents microtubule assembly, impairing neutrophil chemotaxis and migration and inhibiting NLRP3 inflammasome activation and IL-1 beta release.
drugs.sideEffects: Diarrhea, nausea, myopathy and rhabdomyolysis, bone marrow suppression in overdose, peripheral neuropathy
drugs.contraindications: Severe renal or hepatic impairment combined with CYP3A4 or P-glycoprotein inhibitors such as clarithromycin, cyclosporine, or verapamil
drugs.tooltip: In familial Mediterranean fever it prevents both attacks and the AA amyloidosis that causes renal failure, so it is taken lifelong. Fatal toxicity occurs with CYP3A4 inhibitors in renal impairment.

drugs.name: Allopurinol (Rheumatology)
drugs.primaryEffect: Lowers serum urate to dissolve tophi and prevent flares
drugs.treatmentUsage: Chronic gout with recurrent flares, tophi, or urate nephropathy; tumor lysis prophylaxis
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Inhibits xanthine oxidase so hypoxanthine and xanthine are excreted instead of being converted to poorly soluble uric acid.
drugs.sideEffects: Rash, severe hypersensitivity syndrome especially with HLA-B*5801, hepatotoxicity, flares on initiation, cytopenias
drugs.contraindications: Concurrent azathioprine without dose reduction, prior severe hypersensitivity; screen HLA-B*5801 in Han Chinese, Thai, and Korean patients
drugs.tooltip: Treat to a urate target below 6 mg/dL, or below 5 if tophi are present. Start low and titrate, always with colchicine or NSAID prophylaxis for the first three to six months.

drugs.name: Denosumab (Rheumatology)
drugs.primaryEffect: Blocks osteoclast-mediated bone destruction
drugs.treatmentUsage: Osteoporosis including glucocorticoid-induced, erosive rheumatoid arthritis adjunct, bone metastases, giant cell tumor of bone
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Monoclonal antibody against RANK ligand that prevents osteoclast precursor differentiation and activation, mimicking the physiologic decoy receptor osteoprotegerin.
drugs.sideEffects: Hypocalcemia, osteonecrosis of the jaw, atypical femoral fracture, infection, severe rebound vertebral fractures after discontinuation
drugs.contraindications: Hypocalcemia (correct first), pregnancy; never stop without transitioning to a bisphosphonate
drugs.tooltip: The RANK-RANKL-osteoprotegerin axis is the central regulator of bone resorption. In rheumatoid arthritis, RANKL from synovium drives the erosions, which denosumab can halt.

drugs.name: Apremilast
drugs.primaryEffect: Modest anti-inflammatory effect without immunosuppression
drugs.treatmentUsage: Psoriatic arthritis, plaque psoriasis, oral ulcers of Behcet disease
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Inhibits phosphodiesterase-4 in immune cells, raising intracellular cAMP which reduces TNF, IL-17, and IL-23 production while increasing anti-inflammatory IL-10.
drugs.sideEffects: Diarrhea and nausea especially in the first weeks, weight loss, headache, depression and suicidal ideation
drugs.contraindications: Hypersensitivity; caution with history of depression; requires renal dose adjustment
drugs.tooltip: An oral option requiring no laboratory monitoring or tuberculosis screening, because it does not cause meaningful immunosuppression. The tradeoff is much lower efficacy than biologics.

drugs.name: Rituximab (Rheumatology)
drugs.primaryEffect: Depletes B cells driving autoantibody production
drugs.treatmentUsage: ANCA-associated vasculitis induction and maintenance, rheumatoid arthritis after TNF failure, pemphigus vulgaris, membranous nephropathy, immune thrombocytopenia
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Binds CD20 on B lymphocytes, causing their depletion through complement and antibody-dependent cytotoxicity while sparing CD20-negative plasma cells and stem cells.
drugs.sideEffects: Infusion reactions, hepatitis B reactivation, progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy, hypogammaglobulinemia, late-onset neutropenia, blunted vaccine response
drugs.contraindications: Active hepatitis B without prophylaxis, active severe infection, live vaccines
drugs.tooltip: Now equivalent or superior to cyclophosphamide for ANCA vasculitis induction, without the infertility and bladder toxicity. Vaccinate before treatment because responses are blunted for months.

drugs.name: Intravenous Immunoglobulin (Immunology)
drugs.primaryEffect: Replaces antibody or modulates autoimmune inflammation
drugs.treatmentUsage: Primary humoral immunodeficiency, Kawasaki disease, Guillain-Barre syndrome, dermatomyositis, immune thrombocytopenia, toxic shock syndrome
drugs.mechanismOfAction: At replacement doses it provides protective IgG; at high immunomodulatory doses it saturates Fc receptors, neutralizes autoantibodies and superantigens, and inhibits complement.
drugs.sideEffects: Headache and aseptic meningitis, thrombosis, renal failure with sucrose-containing products, anaphylaxis in IgA deficiency, hemolysis, volume overload
drugs.contraindications: Selective IgA deficiency with anti-IgA antibodies, severe renal impairment, hyperviscosity, thrombotic risk
drugs.tooltip: In Kawasaki disease it must be given within 10 days to prevent coronary artery aneurysms. Live vaccines must be deferred for 11 months afterward because passive antibody blocks the response.

drugs.name: Cyclosporine (Rheumatology)
drugs.primaryEffect: Blocks T cell activation in autoimmune disease
drugs.treatmentUsage: Severe psoriasis, refractory rheumatoid arthritis, aplastic anemia, uveitis, atopic dermatitis, transplant rejection
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Binds cyclophilin, and the complex inhibits calcineurin so NFAT cannot be dephosphorylated, blocking transcription of interleukin-2 and T cell clonal expansion.
drugs.sideEffects: Nephrotoxicity, hypertension, gingival hyperplasia, hirsutism, tremor, hyperlipidemia, hyperkalemia, gout
drugs.contraindications: Uncontrolled hypertension, renal dysfunction, malignancy, concurrent PUVA phototherapy in psoriasis
drugs.tooltip: The triad of gingival hyperplasia, hirsutism, and hypertension distinguishes it from tacrolimus on exams. Its dramatic efficacy in psoriasis is limited by cumulative nephrotoxicity.
